title: Rivals & Partners
description: From your course: phrases for talking about competition, rivals, partnerships and working together in business.

items.definition: people or companies that compete with each other for the same customers
items.example: Two of our biggest [business rivals] have just merged, so next year could be tough.
items.exampleRu: Два наших главных конкурента только что объединились, так что следующий год может быть тяжёлым.
items.trap: A rival is a person or company; the competition between them is 'rivalry'. Never 'concurrents'.

items.definition: to try to be more successful than someone else
items.example: As a freelancer, I have to [compete with] big agencies for every client.
items.exampleRu: Как фрилансеру, мне приходится бороться с крупными агентствами за каждого клиента.
items.trap: Use 'with' or 'against' for the rival and 'for' for the prize; don't say 'compete to sb' or 'concur with' (that means agree).

items.definition: to work together with someone to make or achieve something
items.example: Last year we [collaborated] with a local bakery on a Christmas menu.
items.exampleRu: В прошлом году мы вместе с местной пекарней сделали рождественское меню.
items.trap: Use 'with' for the person and 'on' for the project: collaborate with sb on sth. Not 'make collaboration'.

items.definition: the act of working together with other people or organisations
items.example: We're organising the charity run in [collaboration] with a local running club.
items.exampleRu: Мы организуем благотворительный забег совместно с местным беговым клубом.
items.trap: The fixed phrase is 'in collaboration with sb', not 'in collaboration of'; 'a collab' is informal, used for brands and music.

items.definition: people or companies that sell the same things as you or try to win the same thing
items.example: Before I set my prices, I checked what my [competitors] were charging.
items.exampleRu: Прежде чем назначить цены, я посмотрел, сколько берут мои конкуренты.
items.trap: Конкуренты is 'competitors', not 'concurrents'; 'competition' is the contest itself or the competitors as a group.

items.definition: people or groups who compete and strongly dislike each other
items.example: My sister and I were [bitter rivals] at school, but now we're best friends.
items.exampleRu: В школе мы с сестрой были заклятыми соперниками, а теперь лучшие друзья.
items.trap: 'Bitter' here means full of anger and resentment, not горький in taste.

items.definition: to each try to do better than the other person
items.example: Every Christmas, my aunts try to [outdo each other] with bigger and bigger desserts.
items.exampleRu: Каждое Рождество мои тёти пытаются переплюнуть друг друга всё более грандиозными десертами.
items.trap: Don't confuse 'outdo' (do better than) with 'overdo' (do too much); past forms: outdid, outdone.

items.definition: to agree to work together, usually against a shared rival or for a shared goal
items.example: In the board game, my brother and I [formed an alliance] to beat Dad.
items.exampleRu: В настолке мы с братом заключили союз, чтобы обыграть папу.
items.pattern: form an alliance with sb (against sb)
items.trap: Заключить союз is 'form' or 'forge' an alliance; 'union' is for trade unions or groups of countries (the EU).

items.definition: to get a small advantage that helps you do better than others
items.example: I'm doing a data course to [gain a competitive edge] in the job market.
items.exampleRu: Я прохожу курс по анализу данных, чтобы получить преимущество на рынке труда.
items.trap: 'Edge' here means a small advantage, not край; the adjective is 'competitive', not 'competition'.

items.definition: to build a strong working relationship with another person or company
items.example: We've [forged a partnership] with a local gym, so staff get cheaper memberships.
items.exampleRu: Мы наладили партнёрство с местным спортзалом, так что абонементы обходятся сотрудникам дешевле.
items.trap: 'Forge' can also mean подделывать (forge a signature), but with partnership, alliance or friendship it means build something strong.

items.definition: to make yourself do more than you thought you could
items.example: Training for a half marathon taught me to [push myself beyond my limits].
items.exampleRu: Подготовка к полумарафону научила меня выходить за пределы своих возможностей.
collocations: step out of your comfort zone
items.pattern: push yourself (beyond your limits / to do sth)
items.trap: Use a reflexive pronoun ('push myself', not 'push me'), and 'beyond' or 'past' your limits, not 'out of'.
wrong: push myself out of my limits

items.definition: a formal word for a person or group you are competing or fighting against
items.example: When negotiating, I try to see the other side as a partner, not an [adversary].
items.exampleRu: На переговорах я стараюсь видеть в другой стороне партнёра, а не противника.
items.trap: Adversary is formal (in everyday speech say 'opponent' or 'rival'); don't confuse it with 'adversity', which means hard times.

items.definition: to become as good or successful as you are able to be
items.example: I left that job because I felt I'd never [fulfil my potential] there.
items.exampleRu: Я ушёл с той работы, потому что чувствовал, что никогда не смогу реализовать там свой потенциал.
items.trap: 'Realise your potential' is also correct, but 'potential' is uncountable here, so not 'potentials'; US spelling: fulfill.

items.definition: working together and helping each other to do something
items.example: Thanks for your [cooperation] while the office was being renovated.
items.exampleRu: Спасибо за понимание и содействие, пока в офисе шёл ремонт.
items.trap: Don't confuse 'cooperation' (working together) with 'corporation' (a big company); British English also writes 'co-operation'.

items.definition: when rival companies work together in some areas while still competing
items.example: Sharing delivery vans with our rivals sounds odd, but [coopetition] has saved us a fortune.
items.exampleRu: Делить фургоны для доставки с конкурентами звучит странно, но соконкуренция сэкономила нам кучу денег.
items.trap: A business buzzword (cooperation + competition): fine in a meeting or an article, but many people outside business won't know it.

items.definition: a business area where companies compete very hard and without mercy
items.example: I'd love to open a restaurant, but it's such a [cut-throat industry].
items.exampleRu: Мечтаю открыть ресторан, но в этой сфере такая жёсткая конкуренция.
items.trap: Отрасль is 'industry' or 'sector', not 'branch' (a branch is a local office or shop of a company).

items.definition: something you say publicly that is confident and maybe risky
items.example: Saying our app will replace email is a [bold statement] – can we back it up?
items.exampleRu: Сказать, что наше приложение заменит почту, — смелое заявление. Нам есть чем его подкрепить?
items.trap: Заявление is a 'statement' when you say it publicly, but an 'application' when it is a form you fill in.

items.definition: to start a project or business and make it begin to work
items.example: It took us six months to [get our podcast off the ground].
items.exampleRu: Нам понадобилось полгода, чтобы запустить наш подкаст.
collocations: get a business off the ground
items.pattern: get sth off the ground / sth gets off the ground
items.trap: The object goes in the middle: 'get the project off the ground', not 'get off the ground the project'.
wrong: get off the ground our podcast
get our podcast from the ground

items.definition: a serious, determined effort, often by several people working together
items.example: We all made a [concerted effort] to hit the deadline before Christmas.
items.exampleRu: Мы все приложили максимум усилий, чтобы уложиться в срок до Рождества.
items.pattern: make a concerted effort to do sth
items.trap: Today it often just means a determined effort, even by one person: 'I'm making a concerted effort to eat better.'

items.definition: to be able to enter, use or see something
items.example: I still can't [get access to] the shared drive – can you check my permissions?
items.exampleRu: У меня всё ещё нет доступа к общему диску — можешь проверить мои права?
items.pattern: get/have/gain access to sth; access sth (no 'to')
items.trap: Access is uncountable: 'get access to', not 'get an access to'; as a verb it takes no 'to': 'access the drive'.

items.definition: to agree or have the same understanding about something
items.example: Let's have a quick call so everyone is [on the same page] before the launch.
items.exampleRu: Давайте быстро созвонимся, чтобы перед запуском все одинаково понимали задачу.
collocations: get everyone on the same page
items.pattern: be on the same page (about sth)
items.trap: Not 'on one page'. Don't mix it up with 'on the same wavelength' («на одной волне» = think and feel alike).

items.definition: to be more successful or more advanced than your competitors
items.example: Our little start-up is [ahead of the pack] when it comes to customer service.
items.exampleRu: Когда дело касается клиентского сервиса, наш маленький стартап опережает всех.
items.trap: 'Pack' here is a group of competitors, like wolves or runners, not упаковка; a similar idiom is 'ahead of the game'.

items.definition: a decision that is so easy you don't need to think about it
items.example: A four-day week for the same salary? It's a [no-brainer].
items.exampleRu: Четырёхдневка за ту же зарплату? Тут и думать нечего.
items.trap: Informal, and it describes a decision, never a person; for a silly person say 'an idiot' or 'brainless'.

items.definition: to get the good results of something you worked hard for
items.example: After two years of evening classes, I'm finally [reaping the rewards] at work.
items.exampleRu: После двух лет вечерних курсов я наконец пожинаю плоды на работе.
collocations: reap the rewards of hard work
items.trap: Not 'collect the fruits' (a calque of «пожинать плоды»); for bad results people say 'you reap what you sow'.

items.definition: to find the order and position of all the genes in human DNA
items.example: I watched a documentary last night about how scientists [mapped the human genome].
items.exampleRu: Вчера вечером я смотрел документалку о том, как учёные расшифровали геном человека.
items.trap: Расшифровать геном is 'map', 'sequence' or 'decode' it, never 'decrypt' (that's for codes and passwords); a genome is all your genes, not one gene.

items.definition: producing no carbon dioxide overall, or balancing out all that you produce
items.example: By 2030, the company I work for wants to be [carbon zero].
items.exampleRu: Компания, в которой я работаю, хочет к 2030 году выйти на нулевые выбросы углерода.
items.pattern: be/go carbon zero; a carbon-zero building
items.trap: 'Zero carbon' and 'net zero' are also common; углерод is 'carbon', while уголь is 'coal'.

items.definition: all the companies and steps involved in making a product and getting it to the customer
items.example: My new sofa is three weeks late – apparently it's [supply chain] issues.
items.exampleRu: Мой новый диван задерживается уже на три недели — говорят, проблемы с поставками.
items.trap: A noun used as an adjective stays singular: 'supply chain', not 'supplies chain'.

items.definition: because of something, or in order to get or keep it
items.example: Let's not have a meeting just [for the sake of] having one.
items.exampleRu: Давайте не будем устраивать совещание просто ради того, чтобы оно было.
items.pattern: for the sake of sth / of doing sth; for sb's sake
items.trap: Don't drop 'the': 'for the sake of sth', but 'for my sake' (ради меня) has no 'the'.
